title: Magical Realism
description: Magical realism cinematography treats an extraordinary event as ordinary inside a recognizable world: the same window light, the same 35mm coverage, with one impossible fact staged as if it were weather. The camera does not gawk, add a rim, or warp the lens.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A girl sees a monster and the exposure does not change. Snow falls in a kitchen and the practicals stay kitchen practicals.
Wonder is not a lighting cue. If you add shafts, dutch angles, and a choir of haze, you have left the contract.
It is not Dreamcore (liminal rooms, unresolved memory). It is not Altered State (perception smear).
It is not blockbuster spectacle. The world stays real.
One fact does not.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Motivated naturalistic light: window, overcast, a household bulb. 35mm or 50mm, eye level, coverage as if nothing were impossible.
Play the miracle in the same size you would play a kettle. Do not under-light, dutch, or add volumetric spectacle for the impossible beat.
Prompt ordinary light, one impossible fact treated as weather.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a miracle must not become a set-piece. Do not use it for a trip sequence, a liminal corridor, or an effects showcase.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Magical Realism keeps ordinary light and one impossible fact. Dreamcore empties and softens the room.
Altered State warps perception. Southern Gothic can host strange events but its optical problem is heat and decay, not a calmly covered miracle.
If the camera gawks, it is spectacle, not this look.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Dreamcore, Altered State, or gloss: a liminal hall, a smear, or a volumetric miracle. The tell is a lighting change at the impossible beat.
Fix: keep the same key, the same lens height, and stage the impossibility as weather.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Magical Realism in film?
A look that covers extraordinary events with ordinary, motivated light and realist blocking. The camera does not change grammar for the miracle. The world stays recognizable. One fact does not.
Magical Realism vs Dreamcore

Dreamcore is an unresolved liminal interior with childhood light gone wrong. Magical realism is a real town or house with one impossible fact played like weather. Different rooms, different contracts.
When should I use Magical Realism?
When a miracle must not become spectacle. Skip it for trip warps, for empty memory halls, for cosmic scale, or for a lighting cue that announces wonder.
How do I prompt Magical Realism for AI image or video?
Write: Magical-realist image of [Subject], ordinary light, one impossible fact treated as weather, 35mm eye level, no extra rim. Name the room and the single impossibility.
